inspiration.observed_pattern: A recursive CTE starts from selected parent identifiers, follows parent_id links to collect all descendants, and supplies the complete identifier set to a subsequent deletion operation.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a folder-subtree cleanup. A recursive descendant set rooted at one folder feeds MariaDB's nested CTE-selected DELETE ... RETURNING, removing the selected folder and every descendant while preserving its sibling and an unrelated tree; PostgreSQL arrays, routines, schemas, and source identifiers are not copied.

fixture_notes: Folder 20 is the selected subtree root and folder 30 is its child; both are deleted and returned. Folder 40 is a sibling under root 10, and folder 50 belongs to another root, so both remain.
determinism_notes: Folder IDs, parent links, labels, statuses, and the selected root are fixed. The returned deletion rows are compared unordered; the final hierarchy read is ordered by folder ID with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE folder_nodes (folder_id INT PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INT NULL, folder_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, folder_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO folder_nodes VALUES (10, NULL, 'workspace', 'active'), (20, 10, 'reports', 'archived'), (30, 20, 'weekly', 'archived'), (40, 10, 'inbox', 'active'), (50, NULL, 'external', 'active')

steps.sql: DELETE FROM folder_nodes WHERE folder_id IN (WITH RECURSIVE descendants (folder_id) AS (SELECT folder_id FROM folder_nodes WHERE folder_id = 20 UNION ALL SELECT child.folder_id FROM folder_nodes AS child INNER JOIN descendants AS parent ON child.parent_id = parent.folder_id) SELECT folder_id FROM descendants) RETURNING folder_id, parent_id, folder_label, folder_state

checks.sql: SELECT folder_id, parent_id, folder_label, folder_state FROM folder_nodes ORDER BY folder_id
